title: Persona 6 Is Coming to Nintendo Switch 2 — Atlus Confirms the Long-Awaited RPG for Nintendo’s New Console
description: Atlus has confirmed Persona 6 for Nintendo Switch 2, bringing the next mainline Persona RPG to Nintendo’s latest system. No release date has been announced yet.
body:
**Persona 6 is officially coming to Nintendo Switch 2.** ATLUS confirmed the new version during Nintendo Direct 9.9.2026, expanding the game beyond the PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S and PC versions announced earlier this year.

The distinction matters: Persona 6 itself was first unveiled during the Xbox Games Showcase in June. Nintendo’s September Direct did not reveal the game for the first time — it confirmed that **Nintendo Switch 2 is now part of the game’s official platform lineup**.

ATLUS is still keeping most of Persona 6 under wraps. There is no release date yet, but the studio has confirmed an all-new standalone story in a never-before-seen locale, with P-Studio producing the next mainline entry.
author: Rouane Mounssif
imageAlt: Masked character shown in Persona 6 promotional imagery against the game’s green visual backdrop.

contentBlocks.text: The biggest new piece of Persona 6 news from Nintendo Direct 9.9.2026 is straightforward but significant: **ATLUS has added Nintendo Switch 2 to the game’s confirmed platforms**. Persona 6 had previously been announced for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S and PC. The Switch 2 confirmation closes the most obvious gap in the platform lineup and means Nintendo players are included alongside the previously announced versions.
contentBlocks.heading: Persona 6 is officially coming to Nintendo Switch 2
contentBlocks.caption: Persona 6 imagery reflects the green visual identity ATLUS introduced with the next mainline entry.
contentBlocks.imageAlt: Masked character shown against a green backdrop in Persona 6 promotional imagery.
contentBlocks.subtitle: ATLUS / SEGA

contentBlocks.text: Persona 6 was originally announced during the **Xbox Games Showcase in June 2026**. That first teaser established the game’s existence and its initial PlayStation, Xbox and PC platforms. Nintendo’s Direct adds an important new platform rather than re-announcing the project from scratch — an important distinction for anyone following the game’s rollout closely.
contentBlocks.heading: This is a Switch 2 confirmation, not Persona 6’s first reveal

contentBlocks.text: ATLUS has not announced a release date for Persona 6. The current official information lists the launch timing as **TBD**, so any specific date circulating online should still be treated as unconfirmed unless ATLUS or SEGA says otherwise. P-Studio is producing the game, and further details are still being held back.
contentBlocks.heading: There is still no Persona 6 release date

contentBlocks.text: ATLUS describes Persona 6 as a completely new standalone story rather than a direct continuation of Persona 5. Official material says the game takes place in a **never-before-seen locale**, giving the next numbered entry room to establish its own setting, cast and themes while carrying forward the identity of the series.
contentBlocks.heading: Persona 6 is an all-new standalone story

contentBlocks.text: ATLUS has revealed very little about Persona 6’s systems so far. The series is known for mixing everyday life, relationships and supernatural conflict, but Nintendo and ATLUS have not yet detailed how those elements will evolve in the new entry. That makes the Switch 2 confirmation concrete news while most of the game itself remains deliberately mysterious.
contentBlocks.heading: ATLUS is still keeping the new cast and gameplay under wraps

contentBlocks.text: For Nintendo players, the timing is important. Persona 6 is being positioned for Switch 2 while the game is still unreleased, rather than arriving years later as happened with some earlier Persona releases on Nintendo hardware. With Persona 4 Revival also headed to Switch 2, ATLUS is giving Nintendo’s new console a much stronger place in the series’ future.
contentBlocks.heading: The Switch 2 version is a bigger deal than a routine late port
contentBlocks.caption: Persona 4 remains part of ATLUS’ renewed push on Nintendo hardware, with Persona 4 Revival also coming to Switch 2.
contentBlocks.imageAlt: Persona 4 character artwork used to illustrate the series’ broader presence on Nintendo Switch 2.
contentBlocks.subtitle: ATLUS / SEGA

contentBlocks.text: The original Persona 6 teaser immediately stood apart visually, with **green** becoming the dominant color associated with the project. Modern Persona entries have long used distinctive color identities — blue around Persona 3, yellow around Persona 4 and red around Persona 5 — which makes the new direction notable even before ATLUS explains what it means thematically.
contentBlocks.heading: Persona 6’s green aesthetic is still one of its biggest mysteries
contentBlocks.caption: Artwork bringing together characters from across modern Persona games highlights how strongly each entry is associated with its own visual identity.
contentBlocks.imageAlt: Characters from multiple Persona games shown together in series artwork.
contentBlocks.subtitle: ATLUS / SEGA

contentBlocks.text: The Switch 2 announcement settles one major platform question, but most of Persona 6 is still a mystery. ATLUS has not revealed a final release date, fully introduced the new cast, or shown enough combat and exploration to establish how far the sequel will change the Persona formula. For now, the most concrete news is that Nintendo Switch 2 has joined the previously announced PlayStation, Xbox and PC versions.
contentBlocks.heading: What we still do not know about Persona 6

quickRead: Persona 6 is officially coming to Nintendo Switch 2 following Nintendo Direct 9.9.2026.
The game was first announced in June 2026 for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, Windows and Steam; Switch 2 is the newly confirmed platform.
ATLUS still lists the Persona 6 release date as TBD, with P-Studio producing the game.
The next mainline entry features an all-new story and locale, while most of its cast and gameplay remain under wraps.
conclusion: Persona 6 coming to Nintendo Switch 2 removes one of the biggest remaining questions around ATLUS’ next mainline RPG. Nintendo players are no longer waiting to find out whether the game will skip the platform or arrive years later. What they are waiting for now is much more interesting: the cast, the setting, the meaning behind Persona 6’s eerie green identity and, eventually, the release date. Until ATLUS reveals more, the Switch 2 confirmation is a meaningful step in turning Persona 6 from a distant teaser into a game with a much clearer platform future.
conclusionHeading: Persona 6 now has its Nintendo platform — the real reveal is what comes next
